paragraphs.title: David’s Vow to Find a Place for God

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist ask the LORD to remember?

answers: Find a place for the LORD
easy.explanation: David vowed to find a place for the LORD and an habitation for the mighty God of Jacob.
easy.q: What did David vow to do?

easy.explanation: David said he would not give sleep to his eyes or go up into his bed until his vow was fulfilled.
easy.q: What did David refuse to give himself?

answers: They emphasize the seriousness of his vow
They caused him to abandon his vow
They have no connection to his vow
medium.explanation: The psalm remembers both David’s suffering and his determined vow.
medium.q: How do David’s afflictions relate to his vow?

medium.explanation: “Afflictions” refers to David’s sufferings and troubles.

answers: That he find a place for the LORD
That the people honor his greatness
medium.explanation: He would not rest until he found a place for the LORD and His dwelling.
medium.q: What did David require before he would rest?

answers: That David’s vow was a deep commitment
That he desired a life of luxury
challenge.explanation: The repeated references emphasize David’s determination to fulfill his vow.
challenge.q: What do the repeated references to sleep, eyelids, and a bed show?

answers: Finding a holy dwelling for the LORD
challenge.explanation: The passage centers on finding a place for the LORD and the mighty God of Jacob.
challenge.q: What was the central goal of David’s efforts in this passage?

answers: As a task that took priority over rest
As a matter only for the priests
challenge.explanation: David was willing to give up sleep and rest until the place was found.
challenge.q: How is David’s attitude toward the dwelling place of God presented?

paragraphs.title: The Dwelling Place Is Found and Worship Is Called For

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Lo, we heard of it at Ephratah.”
easy.q: Where had the people heard of the LORD’s dwelling place?

easy.explanation: They said, “We will go into his tabernacles.”
easy.q: What did the people say they would do?

easy.explanation: The people would worship at the LORD’s footstool.
easy.q: Before what were they called to worship?

answers: Hearing of the place, finding it, and worshipping
Crowning David, building a city, and sleeping
medium.explanation: The passage moves from hearing about the place to finding it and worshipping there.
medium.q: What order of events appears in this passage?

medium.explanation: “Tabernacles” refers to dwelling places or places of habitation.
medium.q: What does “tabernacles” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: They were called to enter His tabernacles and worship at His footstool.
medium.q: What did the people seek to do after finding the dwelling place?

answers: The ark represents His holy presence
The ark is described only as a weapon
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s rest is mentioned together with “the ark of thy strength,” linking the ark with His holy presence.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the ark and the LORD’s rising into His rest?

answers: They were to participate in worship
They were to stay away from the sanctuary
They were to replace the priests
challenge.explanation: The people are invited to come into the LORD’s dwelling and worship Him.
challenge.q: What does “We will go into his tabernacles: we will worship” show about the people?

answers: That the priests be clothed with righteousness and the saints shout for joy
That the priests fight and the saints hide
That the priests sleep and the saints remain silent
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 asks that the priests be clothed with righteousness and the saints shout for joy.
challenge.q: What request is made concerning the priests and saints?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Kingship to David’s House

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David.”
easy.q: To whom did the LORD swear His promise?

answers: They would sit upon his throne
They would immediately cease to reign
easy.explanation: The LORD promised, “Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”
easy.q: What would happen to David’s descendants?

easy.explanation: Their continuing place on the throne depended on keeping the LORD’s covenant and testimony.
easy.q: What were David’s children required to keep?

answers: They must keep the LORD’s covenant and testimony
medium.explanation: Verse 12 makes keeping the covenant and testimony the condition.
medium.q: What condition is given for David’s children to continue on the throne?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to David’s offspring or descendants.
medium.q: What does “the fruit of thy body” mean?

answers: The first gives the promise and the second gives its condition
The second concerns a subject unrelated to kingship
medium.explanation: Verse 11 presents the promise to David, while verse 12 explains the condition for its continuation.

answers: It is connected with faithfulness to the covenant
It is given without any requirement
challenge.explanation: The continuation of the throne is connected with keeping the LORD’s covenant and testimony.
challenge.q: What does the condition reveal about the promise of kingship?

challenge.explanation: The promise extends to later generations of David’s family.
challenge.q: Who is included in the promise that David’s children shall sit on the throne “for evermore”?

answers: Keeping the testimony is presented as a condition for remaining on the throne
Keeping the testimony ends the kingship
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects continued rule with keeping the LORD’s covenant and testimony.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between David’s throne and keeping the testimony?

answers: The fields of the wood only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “For the LORD hath chosen Zion.”
easy.q: What place did the LORD choose?

easy.explanation: The LORD promised, “I will satisfy her poor with bread.”
easy.q: What did the LORD promise to do for Zion’s poor?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “I will also clothe her priests with salvation.”
easy.q: With what would the LORD clothe Zion’s priests?

answers: Because He chose and desired it
Because it was David’s private residence
medium.explanation: The LORD says He chose Zion and desired it for His habitation.
medium.q: Why is Zion described as the LORD’s dwelling place?

medium.explanation: In this context, “provision” refers to food and sustenance.

answers: Through food, salvation, and joyful singing
Through the building of palaces only
medium.explanation: The LORD promises provision, salvation for the priests, and joy for the saints.
medium.q: How is Zion’s blessing expressed in this passage?

answers: Zion’s blessing includes practical care for the poor
The poor are presented as Zion’s enemies
challenge.explanation: The blessing of Zion includes satisfying her poor with bread.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the poor and Zion’s blessing?

answers: Blessing the provision, satisfying the poor, clothing the priests, and giving joy to the saints
challenge.explanation: The verses progress from provision and bread to salvation and joyful praise.

answers: It is presented as lasting and permanent
challenge.explanation: “This is my rest for ever” emphasizes the lasting nature of His dwelling there.
challenge.q: What does “for ever” suggest about the LORD’s dwelling in Zion?

paragraphs.title: David’s Honor and the Shame of His Enemies

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “There will I make the horn of David to bud.”
easy.q: What would the LORD cause to bud for David?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.”
easy.q: What did the LORD ordain for His anointed?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “His enemies will I clothe with shame.”
easy.q: What would the LORD do to David’s enemies?

medium.explanation: The horn suggests strength and honor, while the lamp suggests prominence and light.
medium.q: What is suggested by the combination of the horn and the lamp?

medium.explanation: Here the horn is a symbol of David’s strength, dignity, and exaltation.
medium.q: What does “horn” symbolize in this context?

answers: David receives honor while his enemies receive shame
They receive exactly the same status
David is shamed while his enemies receive a crown
medium.explanation: David’s crown flourishes, while his enemies are clothed with shame.
medium.q: How do the verses distinguish David from his enemies?

answers: In Zion, the LORD makes David’s horn bud and ordains a lamp for His anointed
Zion is presented as David’s place of exile
Zion has no connection with David’s house
challenge.explanation: The word “there” points back to Zion, where the LORD honors David and his anointed.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Zion and the honor of David’s house?

answers: A reversal of status between the enemies and the king
challenge.explanation: The enemies receive shame, while David’s crown flourishes, showing a sharp reversal of status.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between shame and the flourishing crown show?

answers: The LORD strengthens David and protects the honor of his kingdom
Zion is abandoned after being chosen
challenge.explanation: The conclusion presents David’s exaltation, the lamp for the anointed, and the shame of his enemies.
challenge.q: What is the main idea that concludes these verses?
